question: A train travels 180 km in 3 hours. How long will it take to travel 420 km at the same speed?3014
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When speed is constant, the distance covered is directly proportional to the time taken (D ∝ T).

D₁ ÷ T₁ = D₂ ÷ T₂

180 ÷ 3 = 420 ÷ T₂

T₂ = 420 ÷ 60 = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered initially (D₁) = 180 km

Time taken initially (T₁) = 3 hours

New distance to cover (D₂) = 420 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 Case 1: Initial Journey 
• D = 180 km T = 3 hours Speed = 180 ÷ 3 S = 60 km/hr 
• Case 2: New Journey (Same Speed) 
• D = 420 km T = 420 ÷ 60 = 7 hours 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of the train = D₁ ÷ T₁

⇒ Speed = 180 ÷ 3

⇒ Speed = 60 km/hr

⇒ Time required for 420 km = D₂ ÷ Speed

⇒ Time required = 420 ÷ 60

⇒ Time required = 7 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in Speed & Distance

If the speed of an object is kept constant, the distance covered is directly proportional to the time taken (D₁/T₁ = D₂/T₂).

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. If a journey is divided into multiple segments, Average Speed = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ (T₁ + T₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert a speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply it by 5/18. Conversely, to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
